name: Air Fryer Fish and Chips with Minted Peas

components.name: Crumbed Fish

ingredients.name: Raw boneless skinless cod or haddock fillets

steps: Dry fish. Set flour, egg mixed with mustard, and panko in three bowls. Coat fish flour first, then egg, then panko; discard leftover dredge that touched raw fish.
Lightly brush or spray with measured fish oil. Air fry breaded fish at 195-200 C for 10-15 minutes until crisp and fish reaches 63 C, depending on thickness.
Allocate a quarter of the fish, chips, minted peas and tartar to each meal; store all components apart for best reheating.

Air fry fish and chips to restore crispness; reheat peas separately and add cold tartar only on serving. Freeze breaded uncooked fish separately if kitchen process permits, and assess freezer quality of cooked batches.

components.name: Air-Fried Chips

ingredients.name: Raw floury potatoes cut into batons

steps: Cut potatoes into 1 cm chips and rinse thoroughly. Dry, toss with potato oil, cornflour and salt; air fry at 200 C for 25-30 minutes in batches, shaking often.

components.name: Minted Peas & Tartar
steps: Boil or steam the peas for 2-3 minutes, drain and crush coarsely with butter, mint and lemon. Mix light mayonnaise with pickles and capers as tartar sauce.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
BBC Good Food fish-and-chips air-fryer directions adapted to measured four-serving fish, chips, minted peas and a lighter tartar.
Planning: Air fryer needs several sequential batches; SECONDARY STOVETOP peas.
Freezer: coated fish may freeze; cooked chips turn less crisp; peas freeze well; tartar sauce fresh
Dietary: Fish, wheat, eggs, milk, mustard; sauce may contain egg.

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder, for 3–4 days at most, and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C and reheat leftovers to at least 74°C.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or below for 3-4 days maximum; for many fish and shrimp dishes, prioritize eating within 1-2 days for quality and freeze later-week cooked portions promptly.

Cook fish and crustaceans to 63 C (145 F) or applicable local food-safety standard, and reheat cooked leftovers to 74 C. For crab cakes containing egg binder and purchased cooked crab, reheat to 74 C.
When recipe includes rice, cool rapidly and refrigerate promptly; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.
Freeze in suitable airtight food-safe containers. Defrost in refrigerator, not on counter. Re-crisp breading in an air fryer when possible.
Do not freeze fresh avocado, uncooked tomato/cucumber/cabbage salad, or mayonnaise/yogurt-based dressing unless kitchen-tested separately.
Freezer suitability here describes expected eating quality, not laboratory validated shelf life.
